answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The harbor multiplier is published, charged in pigment, and vertex lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4972 identities would post 4183 proofs and burn roughly 80 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
